content: Virtues lose themselves in self-interest, as streams lose themselves in the sea.
author: François de La Rochefoucauld
sourceWork: Memoirs of the Regency of Anne of Austria
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Water is the softest thing on earth, yet it carves through solid granite. It doesn't fight obstacles; it yields, flows around them, and quietly finds its way to its natural level.

François de La Rochefoucauld understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. When we force outcomes with brute willpower and anxiety, we exhaust ourselves and create unnecessary resistance. Aligning with nature means trusting the timing of things and moving with steady, patient persistence.
reflectionPrompt: What hidden motive, insecurity, or fear might be silently driving your recent reactions?
